docs.text: port-stm32 ¶ kb-core's contracts ( kb::iface ) implemented over the STM32Cube HAL for the STM32 G4, H7, F4 and L4 families: one C++20 library, namespace kb::port::stm32 , that lets any driver written against the kb contracts run on an STM32 without a line of HAL code in the driver. The MCU at a glance ¶ Families STM32G4 (Cortex-M4F, 170 MHz), STM32H7 (Cortex-M7F, up to 550 MHz), STM32F4 (Cortex-M4F, up to 180 MHz), STM32L4 (Cortex-M4F, 80 MHz) ( Families ) SDK STM32Cube HAL and CMSIS device files of each family, fetched unchanged at pinned tags and commits ( SOUP ) HAL modules hal_i2c , hal_spi , hal_uart , hal_gpio , hal_cortex (NVIC), hal_adc , hal_tim , hal_fdcan (G4, H7) or hal_can (F4, L4), hal_rcc ; CMSIS-Core for DWT and ITM RTOS Bare metal ( KB_RTOS=NONE ) or FreeRTOS ( KB_RTOS=FREERTOS ), through kb::rtos Language ISO C++20, no heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no virtual functions Level High (kb-core ADR-0011): bounded building blocks, never a product's safety layer Peripherals and contracts ¶ Peripheral kb contract Type Page I2C1 to I2C4 I2cBus I2cController I2C SPI1 to SPI6 SpiDevice , SpiClockControl SpiBus + SpiDevice SPI USART, UART, LPUART1 UartPort , UartBaudControl , UartTxDrain Uart UART GPIO, EXTI GpioOutput / GpioInput , GpioInterrupt OutputPin / InputPin GPIO and EXTI ADC1 to ADC5 AdcChannel AdcChannel ADC TIM (PWM mode 1) PwmOutput PwmChannel PWM FDCAN (G4, H7), bxCAN (F4, L4) CanBus CanController CAN TIM2/TIM5, DWT, ITM MonotonicClock , BusyWait , LogSink Clock , BusyWait , ItmLogSink , UartLogSink Clock, delay and log The same at a glance: native where the contract maps onto the HAL module or core peripheral, adapted where the port adds its own logic to meet it (the UART's own interrupt handler and receive ring, the SPI clock capped at the interrupt ceiling). Contracts on the STM32 port Figure description and sources Rows are the peripherals I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, ADC, PWM, GPIO, Clock and delay, Log and Pulse output; the columns are the base contract of the peripheral and its extra contracts. Native means the contract maps onto the HAL module or core peripheral named in the cell; adapted means the port adds its own logic to meet it, such as its own UART interrupt handler and receive ring, or an SPI clock capped at the interrupt ceiling. Planned marks a contract or form kb-core has not defined yet, and n/a one that kb-core does not have. Drawn from: docs/model/port-contracts.matrix.yml ; inc/kb/port/stm32/adc.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/can.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/gpio.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/i2c.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/log.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/port.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/pwm.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/spi.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/time.hpp ; inc/kb/port/stm32/uart.hpp ; src/spi.cpp ; src/uart.cpp . Every type satisfies its concepts ( static_assert beside its definition) and converts to the contract's type-erased *Ref ( I2cBusRef , SpiDeviceRef , ...), proven at compile time in kb/port/stm32/port.hpp and at run time in the host tests. What the port does not implement, and why: Not implemented Why DMA The transfers are interrupt driven (CPU copies, no cache maintenance needed); DMA, with the H7 cache rules of Integration , comes later An asynchronous Start/Poll form of the calls Not yet a kb-core contract (planned); the port is built to adopt it ( How the port waits ) UART FIFO mode (G4, H7, L4) Off; at the highest baud rates keep masked sections short Dual-core STM32H7 Refused at configure time ( Integration ) CAN FD frames, CAN filters CanFrame is classic CAN; FDCAN runs in classic mode and accepts every frame into RX FIFO 0 LPTIM, low-power modes, I3C, OCTOSPI, USB kb-core has no contract for them PulseTx Not yet a kb-core contract UART9, USART10 (H7) Not served by the vector file or the instance table yet; USART1 to UART8 and LPUART1 are PWM complementary outputs (CHxN), input capture, encoder mode Beyond PwmOutput ; no kb-core contract Families other than G4, H7, F4, L4 Not built or tested; the CMake device check refuses them Rules that hold everywhere ¶ Every wait is bounded and sleeps : every timeout is at most 2 s, measured on the port's own clock (never HAL_GetTick() ), every operation is ended by its interrupt into a Completion waited on a kb::rtos semaphore, every lock is taken with TryLockFor(timeout) ( How the port waits ). Errors are values : every call returns kb::Status or kb::Result<T> ; the HAL status and the handle's ErrorCode are kept as the vendor code ( Detail() , and LastError() on every object). See Error mapping . Bus recovery : I2C stuck-bus detection and nine-clock recovery on the pins as GPIO; SPI aborted and initialised again after a HAL timeout; FDCAN restarted after bus-off, bxCAN by its automatic bus-off management. Thread safety : a lock per peripheral, bounded; see Thread safety . MISRA boundary : only the boundary files in src/boundary/ (one per HAL component) include HAL or CMSIS headers ( MISRA boundary ). Start ¶ Getting started adds the port to a CMake firmware project; the examples bind the port's self test on one device of each family.

docs.text: Changelog ¶ All notable changes of port-stm32. The format follows Keep a Changelog; versions follow Semantic Versioning (before 1.0 a minor version may break). [Unreleased] ¶ Added ¶ Figures: a matrix of the bus contracts the port implements (native, adapted, planned, not available) on the home page, and a sequence of one transaction through the port on the I2C, SPI, UART and CAN pages, drawn by figkit from models in docs/model/ (light and dark SVG, readable on a phone). CI path filter: a pull request that changes only documentation runs only the docs, handbook and DCO checks; the gate allows the code jobs to be skipped only then. The docs publish only from main and v* tags. DMA ( docs/dma.md ), on kb-core's kb::dma vocabulary: dma.hpp (masters and region tags of each family, RequireStream / RequireStreamReaches , DmaStream over DMA1/DMA2 streams and channels with the NVIC priority written from the board's assignment and read back, every flag serviced by its own clear bit on every interrupt entry, a stop bounded in core cycles that proves EN reads 0, quarantine and Recover() ; DmaTransfer over a leased kb::dma::Buffer ; the cache hooks and the start-time placement and MPU check), spi_dma.hpp ( SpiDmaLink : SPI by DMA through a staging pair per bus, H7 order with TSIZE, frames from min_bytes at the full SCK, Capabilities() , Health() , Limits() and Recover() on SpiBus , SpiLimitsOf ) and adc_stream.hpp ( AdcDmaStream : a timer-triggered scan into a kb::dma::Stream of two frames, OVRMOD 0 with the overrun counted in the drain, the interrupt the only drainer, seqlock publication, supervision, idempotent start, the kernel clock read and never selected, DMA only when the conversion count read back equals the frame, else the one-shot fallback, reported). The DMA vectors of each family dispatch to the started stream. kb-core's DMA conformance suite T1 to T18 runs on the port (its DMA boundary linked against kb-core's host DMA-and-cache model, tests/dma_model/ ), in the AXI ( Maintained ) and D2 ( NonCacheable ) regions; unit and compile-fail tests of the DMA layer. The DMA bench kit: tests/target/dma/dma_bench.cpp (built for the four families by the example project), the procedure for an STM32H7 board with its wiring figures, the evidence form ( docs/assurance/bench/ ). Known limit: kb::dma::Stream needs 64-bit atomics that the Arm GNU toolchain lowers to libatomic calls it does not ship; the bench app carries a weak pair ( tests/target/dma/atomic64.c ) until kb-core keeps 32-bit stamps. Removed ¶ The drivers/ submodules (pcal9555, tmc5160, bno08x), drivers/drivers.lock.yml , the pin-hygiene workflow and driver_adapters.hpp . The example firmware is now port_selftest (the port's self test only); chip drivers are bound through the port in kb-core's examples. A port stands alone and the repository root stays small. Changed ¶ kb-core moves to its republished main with the kb::dma part; tools/kb_core_snapshot.py copies the paths kb-core's tools/layout/layout.py vendor names instead of a list of its own. Port codes 0xFA to 0xFE (DMA error, quarantined, placement, frame too large, priority read-back); MapHalStatus maps placement and priority to NotReady and a frame too large to OutOfRange . An AdcChannel on an instance an ADC stream owns is refused ( Busy ). The interrupt vectors include the DMA streams or channels of the device ( KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS_EXCLUDE keeps one for the application). The FreeRTOS example configuration enables recursive mutexes and the stack high-water mark, which kb-core's FreeRTOS backend now uses. Source layout: every public header has a source file of the same name ( src/adc.cpp for adc.hpp , and so on; irq.hpp and version.hpp are header-only), and the HAL boundary is one file per HAL component in src/boundary/ ( i2c.cpp , spi.cpp , uart.cpp , gpio.cpp , adc.cpp , timer.cpp , can.cpp , time.cpp , log.cpp , error.cpp , state.cpp , vectors.cpp ). The combined files ( adc_pwm.cpp , stm32_*_boundary.cpp ) are gone; time.cpp is split into time.cpp , completion.cpp and log.cpp , i2c_controller.cpp is i2c.cpp and spi_device.cpp is spi.cpp . tools/check_layout.py (preflight and ctest) fails on a header without its source or a file that matches no header. No behaviour change; the MISRA records name the new files. Known limits ¶ The SPI interrupt ceilings are estimates; a bench measurement per family is not yet done. A long critical section or a higher-priority interrupt can still overrun an F4 frame at the ceiling ( BusError ). A shared ADC vector with an application instance on it must be excluded ( KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS_EXCLUDE ); the port does not clear the application instance's flags. No CodeQL MISRA scan of the current code yet (the pull request's CI produces it). Fixed ¶ The UART transmit enable is preceded by a signal fence, so the frame stores cannot move past it (with LTO too). The blocking-wait bound is enabled for any spelling of KB_RTOS and for an installed kb-core's FreeRTOS or host backend; a FreeRTOS build takes KB_PORT_STM32_MIN_RTOS_IRQ_PRIORITY from its FreeRTOSConfig.h, and one that leaves it at 0 fails the configure. The SPI clock actually used is recorded ( Stats().actual_clock_hz ) and lowered selections counted ( clamps ). I2C recovery waits up to 25 ms for SCL to rise before it counts SCL as held and skips the clocks. The TIM2/TIM5 vector switches its NVIC line off when no Clock runs on that timer. SPI interrupt transfers are limited to a per-family SCK ceiling (core / 64 on F4, core / 40 with a FIFO), so the per-byte interrupt cannot overrun the receiver; ActualClockHz() reports the SCK used. An abort makes every device's next frame re-initialise the bus. A wait under FreeRTOS ends by the slept RTOS time even if the port's clock stops (the poll cap alone allowed hours). A vector the port serves for an instance it does not own switches its NVIC line off instead of re-entering; KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS_EXCLUDE leaves named vectors to the application. The HAL time-base check accepts a 100 Hz HAL tick; SetBaud() and the FDCAN restart check it too. RTOS-calling interrupt priorities are checked against KB_PORT_STM32_MIN_RTOS_IRQ_PRIORITY ; the ADC interrupt priority is configurable ( AdcConfig::irq_priority ). H7: the ADC uses the asynchronous kernel clock with a divider that meets 36 MHz when HCLK / 4 is above it. I2C: a failed re-initialisation in recovery leaves the controller not ready (it dereferenced a null instance); a recovery that finds SCL held low sends no clocks and is counted ( scl_held ). The UART transmit frame and the interrupt slot pointers are atomics with release/acquire order. CAN frames received before a Release() are not delivered after the reopen. The interrupt vectors are linked for certain: the vector file is an object library added to every firmware that links the port. Before, it sat in the static archive, a weak reference from the startup file never pulled it in, and every USART, EXTI and TIM2/TIM5 interrupt ran Default_Handler . The example firmware checks with nm after each link that every vector and HAL callback of the port is a strong symbol ( tools/check_vectors.cmake ). Clock::Now() never goes back: a new sample order (wrap count, counter, update flag, counter, wrap count), a sample in which the wrap interrupt ran is taken again, and the interrupt clears the flag and counts the wrap with interrupts masked. The earlier rule stepped forward by 2^32 us and back when the interrupt ran between its reads. Clock::Start() zeroes the counter (it keeps running across a jump from a loader). No wait reads HAL_GetTick() or spins at the caller's priority: I2C, SPI and ADC use the HAL's interrupt APIs, the UART transmits from its own interrupt, CAN receives into a ring from its RX FIFO interrupt; every wait is a Completion on a kb::rtos semaphore, bounded on the port's clock (the DWT before a Clock runs) and by a poll cap, with the operation stopped and the peripheral restored on a timeout. Uart , CanController and AdcChannel refuse EnsureReady() when the HAL time base does not run (the HAL's own init waits use it). UART 7-bit frames: the received word is masked to the data bits (7E1 and 7O1 returned the parity bit in bit 7); 7N1 is refused on F4 (it silently became 8N1). PWM on the clock's timer is refused, and the channels of one timer must share its frequency. Every timeout is at most 2 s ( kMaxTimeout ); HAL_MAX_DELAY and longer values are refused. CAN frames are no longer lost behind a 3-deep hardware FIFO; a FIFO overrun or a full ring is Overflow . I2C: a BUSY flag that stays set with idle lines resets the peripheral (on every family); the handle is restored and the error flags cleared after every failure, PE toggled only while BUSY stays set; TXDR/RXDR flushed and the CR2 transfer fields cleared before every transfer. LastError() , LastFailure() and Stats() are free of data races (interrupt-masked records, atomics); the documentation states that they hold the most recent call by any task. The ADC instance's channel count and the EXTI line table change with interrupts masked (two tasks no longer initialise an instance twice, a handler no longer sees a new callback with an old context). The logic that sat in the boundary files (pin claims, EXTI dispatch, timer ownership, the ADC sharing, the clock wrap count, the UART interrupt's decisions, the ITM wait) moved to the platform-free files. Mutex and semaphore creation failures fail EnsureReady() ( Fault , port code kRtosObject ). A kernel clock that reads 0 Hz is refused ( NotReady , kNoClock ); the H7 I2C4 kernel clock is read from D3; TIMPRE is applied to the timer clock; the H7 ADC clock is refused above 36 MHz; F4 ADC channel 19 is refused. UART Release() keeps the RS-485 DE pin driven low; I2C recovery keeps the configured pull-ups. H7 read-only SPI frames are full duplex (the HAL's receive-only call switched to simplex receive). clang-tidy's configuration is valid for clang-tidy 18 (the host job ran nothing), and the pre-flight fails on a configuration error. Changed ¶ I2cController::WriteRead() writes any number of bytes before the repeated START (was at most 2). A write NACK is Nack ( DataNack ) unless I2cConfig::nack_probe is set; no address-only probe is sent by default and never during EnsureReady() . Uart::write_timeout bounds the whole write (was per 65535-byte chunk); Uart::OnByte() / OnErrors() became OnInterrupt(UartEvent) . Clock::Combine() takes a ClockSample and says whether the sample is consistent. New config fields: I2cConfig::irq_priority , I2cConfig::nack_probe , SpiBusConfig::irq_priority , CanConfig::irq_priority . New interrupt entry points: HandleI2cIrq , HandleSpiIrq , HandleAdcIrq , HandleCanIrq . The port defines the HAL completion callbacks of I2C, SPI, ADC and CAN. Dual-core STM32H7 parts and CORE_CM4 builds are refused. kb-core copy re-pinned to kb-core main ( efd67da ); the snapshot tool copies the whole cmake/ folder and refuses a commit that is not on origin/main . Added ¶ completion.hpp ( Deadline , Completion ), docs/waits.md , docs/integration.md (CubeMX, priorities, RTOS start-up, the H7 cache and DMA rules, dual core), docs/kb-core-dependency.md , docs/misra-review.md . The example under FreeRTOS ( -DEXAMPLE_RTOS=FREERTOS , FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.1.0 pinned) and its CI build for G4. [0.1.0-rc.1] ¶ First release candidate: kb-core's contracts over the STM32Cube HAL for the STM32 G4, H7, F4 and L4 families. Added ¶ I2cController ( I2cBus ): TIMINGR computed from the kernel clock (I2C v2) or ClockSpeed (F4), address and data NACK told apart, stuck-bus detection and nine-clock recovery on the pins as GPIO, one owner per instance, statistics, a bounded lock. SpiBus and SpiDevice ( SpiDevice , SpiClockControl ): GPIO chip selects, per-device mode and clock, frames of any length in 65535-byte chunks with chip select held, abort and re-initialisation after a HAL timeout. Uart ( UartPort , UartBaudControl , UartTxDrain ): the port's own receive interrupt into a 256-byte ring, latched receive errors, a bounded polling writer, RS-485 direction control, LPUART1, separate reader and writer locks. OutputPin and InputPin ( GpioOutput , GpioInput , GpioInterrupt ) with pin claims and EXTI line ownership. AdcChannel ( AdcChannel ): shared instances, calibration on G4, H7 and L4, three sampling classes. PwmChannel ( PwmOutput ): the finest duty steps the 16-bit auto-reload allows, idle level while disabled. CanController ( CanBus ): FDCAN in classic mode (G4, H7) and bxCAN (F4, L4), exact bit timing near 87.5 %, loopback and listen-only modes, bus-off recovery, polls that do not hold off each other. Clock ( MonotonicClock , TIM2 or TIM5 extended to 64 bits), BusyWait (DWT), ItmLogSink and UartLogSink ( LogSink ); the interrupt entry points and an optional vector file. The HAL status and ErrorCode to kb::Status mapping with the vendor code kept in Detail() . The STM32Cube HAL, CMSIS device and CMSIS-Core fetched at pinned tags and commits, checked after the fetch. Host tests over fakes of every HAL call in two family variants, compile-fail tests, header checks; example firmware binding the pcal9555, tmc5160 and bno08x drivers for one device of each family.

SPI interrupt transfers are limited to a per-family SCK ceiling (core / 64 on F4, core / 40 with a FIFO), so the per-byte interrupt cannot overrun the receiver; ActualClockHz() reports the SCK used. An abort makes every device's next frame re-initialise the bus. A wait under FreeRTOS ends by the slept RTOS time even if the port's clock stops (the poll cap alone allowed hours). A vector the port serves for an instance it does not own switches its NVIC line off instead of re-entering; KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS_EXCLUDE leaves named vectors to the application. The HAL time-base check accepts a 100 Hz HAL tick; SetBaud() and the FDCAN restart check it too. RTOS-calling interrupt priorities are checked against KB_PORT_STM32_MIN_RTOS_IRQ_PRIORITY ; the ADC interrupt priority is configurable ( AdcConfig::irq_priority ). H7: the ADC uses the asynchronous kernel clock with a divider that meets 36 MHz when HCLK / 4 is above it. I2C: a failed re-initialisation in recovery leaves the controller not ready (it dereferenced a null instance); a recovery that finds SCL held low sends no clocks and is counted ( scl_held ). The UART transmit frame and the interrupt slot pointers are atomics with release/acquire order. CAN frames received before a Release() are not delivered after the reopen. The interrupt vectors are linked for certain: the vector file is an object library added to every firmware that links the port. Before, it sat in the static archive, a weak reference from the startup file never pulled it in, and every USART, EXTI and TIM2/TIM5 interrupt ran Default_Handler . The example firmware checks with nm after each link that every vector and HAL callback of the port is a strong symbol ( tools/check_vectors.cmake ). Clock::Now() never goes back: a new sample order (wrap count, counter, update flag, counter, wrap count), a sample in which the wrap interrupt ran is taken again, and the interrupt clears the flag and counts the wrap with interrupts masked. The earlier rule stepped forward by 2^32 us and back when the interrupt ran between its reads. Clock::Start() zeroes the counter (it keeps running across a jump from a loader). No wait reads HAL_GetTick() or spins at the caller's priority: I2C, SPI and ADC use the HAL's interrupt APIs, the UART transmits from its own interrupt, CAN receives into a ring from its RX FIFO interrupt; every wait is a Completion on a kb::rtos semaphore, bounded on the port's clock (the DWT before a Clock runs) and by a poll cap, with the operation stopped and the peripheral restored on a timeout. Uart , CanController and AdcChannel refuse EnsureReady() when the HAL time base does not run (the HAL's own init waits use it). UART 7-bit frames: the received word is masked to the data bits (7E1 and 7O1 returned the parity bit in bit 7); 7N1 is refused on F4 (it silently became 8N1). PWM on the clock's timer is refused, and the channels of one timer must share its frequency. Every timeout is at most 2 s ( kMaxTimeout ); HAL_MAX_DELAY and longer values are refused. CAN frames are no longer lost behind a 3-deep hardware FIFO; a FIFO overrun or a full ring is Overflow . I2C: a BUSY flag that stays set with idle lines resets the peripheral (on every family); the handle is restored and the error flags cleared after every failure, PE toggled only while BUSY stays set; TXDR/RXDR flushed and the CR2 transfer fields cleared before every transfer. LastError() , LastFailure() and Stats() are free of data races (interrupt-masked records, atomics); the documentation states that they hold the most recent call by any task. The ADC instance's channel count and the EXTI line table change with interrupts masked (two tasks no longer initialise an instance twice, a handler no longer sees a new callback with an old context). The logic that sat in the boundary files (pin claims, EXTI dispatch, timer ownership, the ADC sharing, the clock wrap count, the UART interrupt's decisions, the ITM wait) moved to the platform-free files. Mutex and semaphore creation failures fail EnsureReady() ( Fault , port code kRtosObject ). A kernel clock that reads 0 Hz is refused ( NotReady , kNoClock ); the H7 I2C4 kernel clock is read from D3; TIMPRE is applied to the timer clock; the H7 ADC clock is refused above 36 MHz; F4 ADC channel 19 is refused. UART Release() keeps the RS-485 DE pin driven low; I2C recovery keeps the configured pull-ups. H7 read-only SPI frames are full duplex (the HAL's receive-only call switched to simplex receive). clang-tidy's configuration is valid for clang-tidy 18 (the host job ran nothing), and the pre-flight fails on a configuration error.

docs.text: I2cController ( I2cBus ): TIMINGR computed from the kernel clock (I2C v2) or ClockSpeed (F4), address and data NACK told apart, stuck-bus detection and nine-clock recovery on the pins as GPIO, one owner per instance, statistics, a bounded lock. SpiBus and SpiDevice ( SpiDevice , SpiClockControl ): GPIO chip selects, per-device mode and clock, frames of any length in 65535-byte chunks with chip select held, abort and re-initialisation after a HAL timeout. Uart ( UartPort , UartBaudControl , UartTxDrain ): the port's own receive interrupt into a 256-byte ring, latched receive errors, a bounded polling writer, RS-485 direction control, LPUART1, separate reader and writer locks. OutputPin and InputPin ( GpioOutput , GpioInput , GpioInterrupt ) with pin claims and EXTI line ownership. AdcChannel ( AdcChannel ): shared instances, calibration on G4, H7 and L4, three sampling classes. PwmChannel ( PwmOutput ): the finest duty steps the 16-bit auto-reload allows, idle level while disabled. CanController ( CanBus ): FDCAN in classic mode (G4, H7) and bxCAN (F4, L4), exact bit timing near 87.5 %, loopback and listen-only modes, bus-off recovery, polls that do not hold off each other. Clock ( MonotonicClock , TIM2 or TIM5 extended to 64 bits), BusyWait (DWT), ItmLogSink and UartLogSink ( LogSink ); the interrupt entry points and an optional vector file. The HAL status and ErrorCode to kb::Status mapping with the vendor code kept in Detail() . The STM32Cube HAL, CMSIS device and CMSIS-Core fetched at pinned tags and commits, checked after the fetch. Host tests over fakes of every HAL call in two family variants, compile-fail tests, header checks; example firmware binding the pcal9555, tmc5160 and bno08x drivers for one device of each family.

docs.text: MISRA boundary and deviations ¶ The port is scanned with the CodeQL MISRA C++:2023 pack and the KB-CPP20 profile pack at level high ( ci-misra.yml , kb-core ADR-0011), on a traced host build and a traced Cortex-M build of inc/ and src/ (the port over the HAL fakes, both family variants: kb_port_stm32_scan ). The boundary ¶ STM32Cube HAL and CMSIS headers are included only by the files of src/boundary/ ( deviations/boundary-files.yml ): one file per HAL component, named after the public header it serves, next to the logic file src/<name>.cpp of the same name ( tools/check_layout.py fails on a header without its source, on a combined file and on a file that matches no header): File HAL areas src/boundary/i2c.cpp hal_i2c ; the I2C HAL callbacks and interrupt entry src/boundary/spi.cpp hal_spi ; the SPI HAL callbacks and interrupt entry src/boundary/uart.cpp hal_uart ; the UART interrupt's register reads and entry src/boundary/gpio.cpp hal_gpio and EXTI, hal_rcc (the port clocks) src/boundary/adc.cpp hal_adc , its callbacks and interrupt entry src/boundary/timer.cpp hal_tim : the PWM channels and the clock's counter share one table of handles src/boundary/can.cpp hal_fdcan (G4, H7) or hal_can (F4, L4), their callbacks and interrupt entry src/boundary/time.cpp hal_cortex (PRIMASK), the HAL tick, SystemCoreClock , DWT src/boundary/log.cpp ITM stimulus port 0 src/boundary/error.cpp The HAL_StatusTypeDef value check against error.hpp src/boundary/state.cpp The one instance of the shared state (includes no HAL header) src/boundary/vectors.cpp The device header's instance macros, for the interrupt vectors Each boundary function converts its arguments, makes one HAL call (or a fixed short sequence) and returns the vendor code; a callback or an interrupt entry finds the owner of the handle and passes the event on. Every decision is in the platform-free files, which include no HAL header and have no deviation : what a code means, retries, recovery and the BUSY reset, locking, timing arithmetic and the waits ( src/time.cpp ), the UART's byte handling, the CAN receive ring, pin claims and the EXTI table ( src/gpio.cpp ), timer ownership and the shared ADC instances ( src/adc.cpp , src/pwm.cpp ), the clock's read rule ( src/clock_read.hpp ) and its wrap count. The layering check ( ci-layering.yml ) enforces the boundary, and its poison build compiles the platform-free code with every HAL header replaced by one that stops the build. Records ¶ Id Guideline Where Why How the risk is held DEV-001 Rule 6.7.1 (local variables with static storage) the I2C, SPI, UART, ADC, timer, CAN and shared-state boundary files The HAL keeps each peripheral's state in a handle that outlives each call and is reached from the interrupt handlers and HAL callbacks, and no HAL type may reach a public header: the handles live in one function-local static table per peripheral, and the one instance of the platform-free shared state ( src/state.hpp ) in the same form One accessor per table in an anonymous namespace; entries written by the owner's EnsureReady() , cleared by Release() ; a second owner refused with Busy ; entries shared with an interrupt are atomic and changed only with interrupts masked ( IrqGuard ); every accessor exercised by the host tests DEV-002 Rule 8.2.3 (casts that remove const) the I2C boundary file, one call HAL_I2C_Master_Seq_Transmit_IT takes uint8_t* for data it only reads; the contract hands the port std::span<const uint8_t> , and a write cannot be split into copies One call site; the pinned HAL only reads through the pointer; the tests check the bytes reach the bus and the caller's buffer is unchanged DEV-003 Rule 10.2.3 (unscoped enum without a fixed underlying type) the I2C boundary file, two stores in I2cRestore I2C_HandleTypeDef::State and ::Mode are volatile fields of the HAL's unscoped enumerations; the pinned HAL has no call that returns a handle to ready without a re-initialisation Only the field's own enumerators are stored (no conversion); bus lock held and the instance's interrupts disabled; the tests start a transfer from ready after a NACK, a timeout and a recovery The records are in deviations/deviations.yml . A marker // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(DEV-001) stands on the line before each finding it covers. A clang-tidy suppression of a check the MISRA matrix relies on names its record inside the comment, never as its first or last word (a bare id there would be read as a CodeQL marker): // NOLINTNEXTLINE(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-const-cast): DEV-002, the HAL lacks the const . A marker that covers nothing, an unknown id or a lapsed record ( review_by passed) fails the scan. Findings avoided by design ¶ Guideline What the HAL would have needed What the port does instead Rule 8.2.5 ( reinterpret_cast ) HAL_UART_Transmit takes uint8_t* for log text UartLogSink converts each character with std::bit_cast into a byte buffer Rule 24.5.2 ( memcpy ) Copying frames and text with memcpy std::array assignment and element loops Rule 8.2.6 ( void* to object pointer) HAL handles in public headers Handles stay in the boundary files' tables; the HAL's void* callbacks are not used Rule 10.2.3 ( HAL_StatusTypeDef cast to void ) Discarding the result of HAL_SPI_Abort , HAL_ADC_Stop , HAL_FDCAN_Stop , HAL_CAN_Stop , HAL_CAN_ResetError Each result is used: folded into the reported status or ErrorCode , or compared with HAL_OK (the CAN error callback) Rule 10.2.3 ( IRQn_Type stored through a reference) An out-parameter pair for the I2C event and error vectors I2cEventIrq() and I2cErrorIrq() return each vector by value Rule 8.2.6 in the HAL callbacks Recovering the owner from the handle through a void* user field Each callback finds its owner by comparing the handle's address with the port's table Advisory findings left ¶ Guideline Where Why it stays Rule 6.5.1 (external linkage not declared in a header) The interrupt vectors in src/boundary/vectors.cpp ; the HAL callbacks the port defines (I2C, SPI, ADC, CAN) The vector names are fixed by the startup file's table, which declares them weak; the callback names and signatures are the HAL's (declared in its headers); the entry points are declared in irq.hpp Rule 10.1.1 (parameter could be const) The HAL callbacks Their signatures are the HAL's Advisory findings are reported and do not block. docs.text: DMA ¶ The port's DMA layer: SPI by DMA through port-owned staging buffers, and a timer-triggered ADC scan streamed by circular DMA. It implements kb-core's kb::dma vocabulary (regions, buffers and leases, cache hooks, streams, capabilities, stream assignments) for the STM32 DMA1/DMA2 engines. This page is the port's DMA record in the fixed form: regions, masters, rules, errata handled, the conformance result per case, and what was bench verified. Header What kb/port/stm32/dma.hpp Masters, region tags, the assignment checks, DmaStream (one stream or channel), DmaTransfer<Region> (one leased buffer transfer), PortCacheOps , HandleDmaIrq kb/port/stm32/spi_dma.hpp SpiDmaLink<Region, Bytes> : the two streams and the staging pair of one SPI bus ( SpiBus::AttachDma ) kb/port/stm32/adc_stream.hpp AdcDmaStream<Frame, Region> : an ADC scan into kb::dma::Stream<Frame, 2, Region> , with its one-shot fallback Regions and masters ¶ kb-core knows policies, not addresses. The port's region tags carry the policy, the line, the alignment unit, the masters that reach the memory, and its window ( kBase , kSize ) for the start-time placement check. A board narrows a window by defining its own tag with the same members (the board generator writes them from board.yml ). Tag Memory Policy Line / unit Masters h7::D2Sram D2 SRAM1 to SRAM3 behind a non-cacheable MPU region NonCacheable ( the default H7 region ) 1 / 32 B DMA1, DMA2, MDMA h7::AxiSram AXI SRAM (D1), write-back cached Maintained 32 / 32 B DMA1, DMA2, MDMA h7::Sram4 D3 SRAM4 behind a non-cacheable MPU region NonCacheable 1 / 32 B BDMA, DMA1, DMA2, MDMA h7::Dtcm DTCM Coherent 1 / 4 B MDMA only (declared so a DMA½ buffer there fails to build) Sram Main SRAM of F4, G4, L4 (no data cache) Coherent 1 / 4 B DMA1, DMA2 Masters are kMasterDma1 , kMasterDma2 , kMasterBdma , kMasterMdma . The port drives DMA1 and DMA2 only; BDMA and MDMA are in the model so the checks can refuse them. In a kb::dma::StreamAssignment , engine 1 is DMA1 and 2 is DMA2; the stream is 0 to 7 on F4 and H7 and the channel 1 to 8 on G4 and L4; the request is the DMAMUX request line (G4, H7, L4+), the CHSEL channel selection (F4) or the CSELR value (L4). The cache hooks ( PortCacheOps ) clean and invalidate by 32-byte line through SCB->DCCMVAC and SCB->DCIMVAC on the Cortex-M7 when its D-cache is on, and are barriers only on the cacheless families. kb::dma::Buffer hands them whole lines it owns, so an invalidate never reaches a neighbour. Rules the port keeps ¶ Caller memory is never a DMA target. SpiDevice::Transfer copies through the bus's staging pair; zero-copy is only DmaTransfer over a typed kb::dma::Buffer . Assignment, not search. A stream comes from the board's StreamAssignment ; RequireStream<S>() and RequireStreamReaches<S, Region>() check it at compile time, EnsureReady() again at start (engine, stream, request range, interrupt tier, a stream already enabled by someone else is refused). The port writes the NVIC priority of each stream from the assignment in EnsureReady() and reads it back; a read-back that differs is refused ( NotReady , port code 0xFE ). A vendor code generator that rewrote the priority cannot go unnoticed. Every interrupt entry services every flag of its stream (transfer error, direct-mode error, FIFO error, half, complete: errors first), each cleared by its own clear bit and counted, whether a transfer is in flight or not ( DmaStats::unexpected ). Nothing is left set to re-assert the interrupt. CGIF is never written. Confirmed stop. A stop clears EN and waits for EN to read 0, bounded by sdk::DmaStopBoundCycles() (10 µs of core cycles, never below 1024) and by the same number of reads. Only then does the memory return to the CPU; a stop that is not confirmed quarantines the buffer, the stream is Faulted and refuses transfers until Recover() (control register cleared, EN proven 0). Exactly once. Completion, cancellation and the report meet in a kb::dma::CompletionLatch . Fallback is never silent. Capabilities() and Health() of SpiBus , DmaStream , DmaTransfer and AdcDmaStream say which path serves; an ADC stream on its fallback flags every frame Fallback() . Start-time placement. SpiBus::EnsureReady() and AdcDmaStream::Start() refuse ( NotReady , port code 0xFC ) a buffer outside its region's window, and a NonCacheable region that no enabled MPU region makes uncached while the D-cache is on ( MPU->RNR/RBAR/RASR read back). Default H7 region: the D2 window. Staging buffers and ADC rings go to h7::D2Sram unless a board chooses h7::AxiSram for a buffer ( Maintained , cleaned and invalidated by line). SPI ¶ Item Behaviour Which frames SpiDmaConfig::min_bytes (default 16) and up by DMA at the device's SCK; shorter by interrupt at the interrupt ceiling Order, H7 (SPI with TSIZE) SPE cleared and TSIZE written, RXDMAEN, receive stream, transmit stream, TXDMAEN, SPE, CSTART Order, F4, G4, L4 RXDMAEN, receive stream, transmit stream, TXDMAEN, SPE End The receive stream's completion ends the frame; the transmit stream may run with errors-only interrupts ( IrqUse::ErrorsOnly ) and is concluded from its registers; the requests are disabled, SPE cleared on H7 Size One pass of at most the staging capacity; larger frames OutOfRange (no silent cut). SpiLimitsOf<Link> with kb::dma::RequireBusCarries checks drivers at compile time Errors Stream error: Fault (port code 0xFA and the flags). SPI overrun or mode fault: BusError . Deadline: both streams stopped with proof, Timeout . Unconfirmed stop: Fault ( 0xFB ) until SpiBus::Recover() Priorities Both streams at the SPI interrupt's priority (refused otherwise): an error and a completion of one frame never preempt each other ADC scan stream ¶ Item Behaviour Hardware Scan of the configured ranks at each rising edge of the board's trigger timer ( trigger : the family's ADC_EXTERNALTRIG_* ); circular DMA over a two-frame ring ( Frames = 2 ) Overrun OVRMOD = 0 (data preserved: the requests stop visibly); OVR read and cleared in the drain and counted with OnOverrun (never a frame); the restart reads it as the stop reason; no OVR or EOC interrupt Drainer The stream's interrupt only (the owner never reads the flags); halves published oldest first; a half the DMA lapped (both flags pending, or the transfer counter inside it after its copy) is published Torn Owner Service() : at most frames_per_pass frames, the latest published through a seqlock ( Latest() for any task), then Stream::Supervise (signed stall time, restart, back-off, fallback) Start After the scheduler (refused while the HAL time base does not run); idempotent; refused when the ADC kernel clock reads 0 (the port never writes the kernel-clock multiplexer); the instance is the stream's alone (an AdcChannel on it is refused, and the other way round) DMA or fallback DMA only when a stream is assigned and the conversion count read back from the sequence register equals StreamShape.elements ; otherwise the one-shot fallback (each Service() converts every rank by interrupt), reported in FallbackReason() , Mode() , Capabilities() , Health() and every frame Calibration Offset and linearity on H7, offset on G4 and L4, none on F4 64-bit atomics on Cortex-M (known limit) ¶ kb::dma::Stream keeps its frame time stamp in a std::atomic<uint64_t> . A 32-bit Cortex-M has no 64-bit atomic load or store, the Arm GNU toolchain lowers them to calls of __atomic_load_8 and __atomic_store_8 , and it ships no libatomic : a firmware that uses AdcDmaStream does not link without them. The port library does not provide them (they are reserved names taking a pointer to void, which would need a MISRA deviation in the port). docs.text: The port's DMA layer: SPI by DMA through port-owned staging buffers, and a timer-triggered ADC scan streamed by circular DMA. It implements kb-core's kb::dma vocabulary (regions, buffers and leases, cache hooks, streams, capabilities, stream assignments) for the STM32 DMA1/DMA2 engines. This page is the port's DMA record in the fixed form: regions, masters, rules, errata handled, the conformance result per case, and what was bench verified. docs.text: kb-core knows policies, not addresses. The port's region tags carry the policy, the line, the alignment unit, the masters that reach the memory, and its window ( kBase , kSize ) for the start-time placement check. A board narrows a window by defining its own tag with the same members (the board generator writes them from board.yml ). Tag Memory Policy Line / unit Masters h7::D2Sram D2 SRAM1 to SRAM3 behind a non-cacheable MPU region NonCacheable ( the default H7 region ) 1 / 32 B DMA1, DMA2, MDMA h7::AxiSram AXI SRAM (D1), write-back cached Maintained 32 / 32 B DMA1, DMA2, MDMA h7::Sram4 D3 SRAM4 behind a non-cacheable MPU region NonCacheable 1 / 32 B BDMA, DMA1, DMA2, MDMA h7::Dtcm DTCM Coherent 1 / 4 B MDMA only (declared so a DMA½ buffer there fails to build) Sram Main SRAM of F4, G4, L4 (no data cache) Coherent 1 / 4 B DMA1, DMA2 Masters are kMasterDma1 , kMasterDma2 , kMasterBdma , kMasterMdma . The port drives DMA1 and DMA2 only; BDMA and MDMA are in the model so the checks can refuse them. In a kb::dma::StreamAssignment , engine 1 is DMA1 and 2 is DMA2; the stream is 0 to 7 on F4 and H7 and the channel 1 to 8 on G4 and L4; the request is the DMAMUX request line (G4, H7, L4+), the CHSEL channel selection (F4) or the CSELR value (L4). The cache hooks ( PortCacheOps ) clean and invalidate by 32-byte line through SCB->DCCMVAC and SCB->DCIMVAC on the Cortex-M7 when its D-cache is on, and are barriers only on the cacheless families. kb::dma::Buffer hands them whole lines it owns, so an invalidate never reaches a neighbour.

docs.text: Caller memory is never a DMA target. SpiDevice::Transfer copies through the bus's staging pair; zero-copy is only DmaTransfer over a typed kb::dma::Buffer . Assignment, not search. A stream comes from the board's StreamAssignment ; RequireStream<S>() and RequireStreamReaches<S, Region>() check it at compile time, EnsureReady() again at start (engine, stream, request range, interrupt tier, a stream already enabled by someone else is refused). The port writes the NVIC priority of each stream from the assignment in EnsureReady() and reads it back; a read-back that differs is refused ( NotReady , port code 0xFE ). A vendor code generator that rewrote the priority cannot go unnoticed. Every interrupt entry services every flag of its stream (transfer error, direct-mode error, FIFO error, half, complete: errors first), each cleared by its own clear bit and counted, whether a transfer is in flight or not ( DmaStats::unexpected ). Nothing is left set to re-assert the interrupt. CGIF is never written. Confirmed stop. A stop clears EN and waits for EN to read 0, bounded by sdk::DmaStopBoundCycles() (10 µs of core cycles, never below 1024) and by the same number of reads. Only then does the memory return to the CPU; a stop that is not confirmed quarantines the buffer, the stream is Faulted and refuses transfers until Recover() (control register cleared, EN proven 0). Exactly once. Completion, cancellation and the report meet in a kb::dma::CompletionLatch . Fallback is never silent. Capabilities() and Health() of SpiBus , DmaStream , DmaTransfer and AdcDmaStream say which path serves; an ADC stream on its fallback flags every frame Fallback() . Start-time placement. SpiBus::EnsureReady() and AdcDmaStream::Start() refuse ( NotReady , port code 0xFC ) a buffer outside its region's window, and a NonCacheable region that no enabled MPU region makes uncached while the D-cache is on ( MPU->RNR/RBAR/RASR read back). Default H7 region: the D2 window. Staging buffers and ADC rings go to h7::D2Sram unless a board chooses h7::AxiSram for a buffer ( Maintained , cleaned and invalidated by line).

docs.text: kb::dma::Stream keeps its frame time stamp in a std::atomic<uint64_t> . A 32-bit Cortex-M has no 64-bit atomic load or store, the Arm GNU toolchain lowers them to calls of __atomic_load_8 and __atomic_store_8 , and it ships no libatomic : a firmware that uses AdcDmaStream does not link without them. The port library does not provide them (they are reserved names taking a pointer to void, which would need a MISRA deviation in the port). The bench app carries a weak pair ( tests/target/dma/atomic64.c : interrupts masked for the two word accesses, correct on a single core) that an application may copy until kb-core keeps the time stamp in 32-bit atomics.

docs.text: Examples ¶ examples/stm32/ is one CMake firmware project for the four families: EXAMPLE_BOARD picks the device, its linker script, its HAL configuration and its pins ( boards/<board>/ ). It builds port_selftest.elf : a self test of the port: Clock , BusyWait , ItmLogSink , a PwmChannel at 5 kHz and 25 %, an AdcChannel read in millivolts, a CanController in internal loopback (one frame sent and received back), a Uart write; an idle loop: bare metal ( KB_RTOS=NONE ) by default, or one FreeRTOS task with -DEXAMPLE_RTOS=FREERTOS (FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.1.0 fetched at its pinned commit, freertos/FreeRTOSConfig.h , src/freertos_start.c ; the HAL tick from the kernel's tick hook, every object started in the task). docs.text: Getting started ¶ 1. Add the port to a CMake firmware project ¶ The port is a CMake project; add_subdirectory it from the application's CMakeLists.txt with the device and the folder of the application's stm32<family>xx_hal_conf.h . The HAL, CMSIS device and CMSIS-Core are fetched at their pinned commits; the startup file of the device is handed back in KB_PORT_STM32_STARTUP . cmake_minimum_required ( VERSION 3.25 ) project ( app C CXX ASM ) set ( KB_PORT_STM32_DEVICE STM32G474xx CACHE STRING "" ) set ( KB_PORT_STM32_HAL_CONF_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/board" CACHE PATH "" ) add_subdirectory ( third_party/port-stm32 port-stm32 ) add_executable ( app.elf src/main.cpp "${KB_PORT_STM32_STARTUP}" ) target_link_libraries ( app.elf PRIVATE kb::port_stm32 ) target_link_options ( app.elf PRIVATE -T ${ CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR } /board/linker.ld -specs=nano.specs -specs=nosys.specs -Wl,--gc-sections ) Configure with an Arm GNU toolchain file; cmake/arm-none-eabi.cmake is one ( -DKB_ARM_CORE=cortex-m7f for H7): cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE = third_party/port-stm32/cmake/arm-none-eabi.cmake cmake --build build The HAL configuration must enable the modules the port uses: HAL_MODULE_ENABLED and the I2C , SPI , UART , GPIO , DMA , RCC , CORTEX , PWR , ADC , TIM , EXTI and FDCAN (G4, H7) or CAN (F4, L4) modules. The examples' examples/stm32/boards/*/stm32*_hal_conf.h include ST's template unchanged, which enables every module. KB_RTOS selects the kb::rtos backend: NONE (bare metal, the default off ESP-IDF) or FREERTOS with KB_FREERTOS_INCLUDE_DIRS naming the kernel's headers (kb-core includes them as freertos/<header>.h ; cmake/kb_port_stm32_freertos.cmake fetches the pinned FreeRTOS-Kernel and provides that layout, as the example does with -DEXAMPLE_RTOS=FREERTOS ). KB_RTOS=NONE has no scheduler: kb-core's none backend is deterministic with a fake tick, its SleepFor does not sleep on silicon, and a semaphore take cannot block. The port's waits then poll their completion, still bounded on the port's clock ( How the port waits ). Use FreeRTOS when a task must sleep while it waits. 2. Create the objects ¶ #include "kb/port/stm32/port.hpp" namespace stm = kb :: port :: stm32 ; stm :: I2cConfig MakeI2c () { stm :: I2cConfig c {}; c . instance = 1U ; c . scl = stm :: PinId { stm :: GpioPort :: B , 8U , 4U }; // PB8, AF4 c . sda = stm :: PinId { stm :: GpioPort :: B , 9U , 4U }; // PB9, AF4 c . clock_hz = 400000U ; return c ; } // Under FreeRTOS: the first task, after the scheduler runs. Bare metal: from main(). void AppMain () { static stm :: Clock clock {}; static_cast < void > ( clock . Start ()); // first: every wait of the port is measured on it static stm :: I2cController bus { MakeI2c ()}; // static: drivers keep references if ( bus . EnsureReady () != kb :: Status :: Ok ) { // bus.LastError().Detail(): HAL status in bits 0..7, ErrorCode from bit 8 } const std :: array < uint8_t , 2 > tx { 0x06U , 0x00U }; const kb :: Status s = bus . Write ( 0x20U , tx ); // NoDevice, Nack, Timeout, BusError, Busy ... } Objects keep their configuration and touch no hardware until EnsureReady() ( Start() for the clock). Call it once from one context before the object is shared, after the scheduler runs (it creates the object's kb::rtos mutexes and semaphores), never from a static constructor and never with interrupts masked; after that every member is safe to call from several tasks ( Thread safety ). Start the Clock first: until a Clock runs, the port measures its waits on the DWT cycle counter. 3. The HAL time base ¶ The port's waits never read HAL_GetTick() . The HAL's own initialisation code still does ( HAL_UART_Init , the ADC enable, the CAN initialisation and start), so its time base must run, and Uart , AdcChannel and CanController refuse EnsureReady() with NotReady (port code kHalTickStopped ) when it does not: Setup HAL time base Bare metal SysTick_Handler calling HAL_IncTick() (what HAL_Init() sets up) FreeRTOS FreeRTOS owns SysTick_Handler ( xPortSysTickHandler ), so the application must not define one. Give the HAL a time base of its own: a TIMx whose update interrupt calls HAL_IncTick() (CubeMX's "Timebase Source" setting, HAL_InitTick() overridden), or HAL_IncTick() from vApplicationTickHook() as the example does Either way, call EnsureReady() only from task context with interrupts enabled. A HAL tick advanced at 100 Hz (a FreeRTOS tick hook at configTICK_RATE_HZ = 100) is accepted. Under FreeRTOS set KB_PORT_STM32_MIN_RTOS_IRQ_PRIORITY to configLIBRARY_MAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY : the port then refuses an interrupt priority the kernel does not mask ( Integration ). 4. Interrupts ¶ The port defines the vectors of the peripherals it serves and the HAL completion callbacks of I2C, SPI, ADC and CAN; a CubeMX project leaves those peripherals unconfigured and drops the generated handlers and callbacks ( Integration ). The default priorities (5) suit FreeRTOS with configLIBRARY_MAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY = 5. 5. Bind a driver ¶ A driver's port is a thin adapter from its hooks to the kb contracts. Write it as a template over the contracts, so the same adapter runs over this port, another MCU port, a host fake or a *Ref chosen at run time. Worked adapters for real drivers live in kb-core's examples, not in this repository. Building the host tests ¶ cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DKB_PORT_STM32_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure No HAL and no Arm toolchain are needed: the boundary files build against fakes of every HAL call they make ( Testing and CI ).

docs.text: Integration: CubeMX, interrupts, RTOS and caches ¶ What the port owns ¶ The port owns the HAL handles of every peripheral instance it opens (they live in its boundary files), the interrupt vectors of those peripherals, and these HAL callbacks, which it defines (they are weak in the HAL): Peripheral HAL callbacks the port defines I2C HAL_I2C_MasterTxCpltCallback , HAL_I2C_MasterRxCpltCallback , HAL_I2C_ErrorCallback , HAL_I2C_AbortCpltCallback SPI HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback , HAL_SPI_TxRxCpltCallback , HAL_SPI_ErrorCallback ADC HAL_ADC_ConvCpltCallback , HAL_ADC_ErrorCallback FDCAN (G4, H7) HAL_FDCAN_RxFifo0Callback , HAL_FDCAN_TxBufferCompleteCallback bxCAN (F4, L4) HAL_CAN_RxFifo0MsgPendingCallback , HAL_CAN_ErrorCallback , HAL_CAN_TxMailbox{0,1,2}CompleteCallback , HAL_CAN_TxMailbox{0,1,2}AbortCallback Each callback looks up the handle in the port's table and does nothing for a handle the port does not own. The UART, EXTI and clock interrupts do not use HAL callbacks: the port's own handlers read the registers. With USE_HAL_*_REGISTER_CALLBACKS set to 1 in the HAL configuration, HAL_*_Init installs these same functions as the handle's callbacks, so the port works either way. A CubeMX project ¶ The vectors. With KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS=ON (the default) the port's vector file defines every USART/UART/LPUART, I2C event and error, SPI, ADC, FDCAN line 0 or bxCAN TX/RX0/SCE, EXTI and TIM2/TIM5 vector the device has, whether or not a port object uses the instance. For a peripheral CubeMX (or other code) keeps, name its vectors in KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS_EXCLUDE (for example -DKB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS_EXCLUDE="USART1_IRQHandler" ): the port does not define them, and the generated handlers stay. A vector the port serves for an instance no port object owns switches its NVIC line off at the first interrupt (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN, a shared ADC vector with no open instance), so a peripheral left enabled by other code cannot make it re-enter forever; that peripheral then gets no interrupts, so exclude its vectors. EXTI lines are grouped in vectors ( EXTI9_5 , EXTI15_10 ): a line no InputPin owns is cleared and not served; to serve a line of the application, exclude the vector and call HandleExtiIrq() from the application's handler for the port's lines. KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS=OFF drops the whole file. The clock's TIM2 / TIM5 vector switches its NVIC line off when no Clock runs on that timer. A shared ADC vector ( ADC1_2 on G4 and L4, ADC on F4 and H7) with one instance the port's and another the application's must be excluded: the application's handler then calls HandleAdcIrq() for the port's instances and HAL_ADC_IRQHandler() for its own (the port switches a shared vector off only when none of its instances is open). A vector defined twice is a link error, never a silent override; tools/check_vectors.cmake checks after the link that every vector the port defines is its strong symbol (an excluded one is not checked). Leave the port's peripherals unconfigured in CubeMX (no init code, no NVIC entry): the port initialises them in EnsureReady() . Drop the generated callback functions listed above. Drop the HAL_*_MspInit / HAL_*_MspDeInit bodies of the port's peripherals: the port configures its pins itself, and an MspDeInit that resets pins would run on every SPI mode change ( SpiConfigure re-initialises). The HAL time base : with FreeRTOS, CubeMX moves the HAL time base off SysTick to a TIMx (often at the lowest priority). That is fine for the port, whose waits never read it; but it must run whenever tasks run, because the HAL's own initialisation waits read it (see How the port waits ). Never call EnsureReady() inside a critical section or with BASEPRI raised. Interrupt priorities ¶ NVIC priority numbers are the unshifted ones of HAL_NVIC_SetPriority (0 to 15 with 4 priority bits). Under FreeRTOS, an interrupt that calls the RTOS must have a priority number at or above (that is, at or below in urgency) configLIBRARY_MAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY : Interrupt Default Calls the RTOS UART ( UartConfig::irq_priority ) 5 Yes (a semaphore give) I2C event and error ( I2cConfig::irq_priority ) 5 Yes SPI ( SpiBusConfig::irq_priority ) 5 Yes ADC ( AdcConfig::irq_priority , the instance's first channel's) 5 Yes CAN ( CanConfig::irq_priority ) 5 Yes EXTI ( InputConfig::irq_priority ) 5 Only if the application's callback does Clock wrap ( ClockConfig::irq_priority ) 1 No (it may stay above the syscall limit) The defaults match configLIBRARY_MAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY = 5, the value in the example's FreeRTOSConfig.h and a common one. Set KB_PORT_STM32_MIN_RTOS_IRQ_PRIORITY (CMake) to that value: EnsureReady() of Uart , I2cController , SpiBus , AdcChannel and CanController then refuses an irq_priority below it, or above 15, with InvalidArgument , so no RTOS-calling interrupt can run above the syscall limit. It is 0 by default (bare metal: no limit); the FreeRTOS example sets 5. EXTI and the clock wrap are not checked (their handlers do not call the RTOS unless the application's EXTI callback does). RTOS objects and start-up order ¶ EnsureReady() creates the object's kb::rtos mutexes and semaphores. Call it after the scheduler runs (in the first task), never from a static constructor: an RTOS object created before the scheduler can leave BASEPRI raised until the scheduler starts, which stops the HAL time base. The example under EXAMPLE_RTOS=FREERTOS does this. Caches and DMA (H7) ¶ Interrupt-driven transfers are CPU copies: they need no cache maintenance, and caller buffers may be anywhere the CPU can reach, D-cache on or off. DMA transfers ( DMA ) never use a caller buffer: they go through port-owned kb::dma::Buffer s the board places in a DMA region. The board's start-up owns the MPU (the D2 window: one region, non-cacheable, shareable) and the caches; the port reads the MPU back at start and refuses a mismatch. A board's DMA buffer sections are loaded like .data (a kb::dma::Buffer holds its data address), not NOLOAD. The port's DMA vectors ( DMA1_Stream0_IRQHandler ... or DMA1_Channel1_IRQHandler ...) dispatch to the started DmaStream and disable the line of a stream the port does not own. An application that keeps a DMA vector for itself names it in KB_PORT_STM32_VECTORS_EXCLUDE and calls kb::port::stm32::HandleDmaIrq(engine, stream) for the port's streams. The rules behind the DMA layer on STM32H7 (observed with an earlier implementation on STM32H7 hardware): DMA buffers are 32-byte aligned and sized to whole cache lines; the D-cache is cleaned before a transmit and invalidated before the CPU reads received data, or the buffers are in an MPU region marked non-cacheable; invalidating the D-cache after a CPU copy into a cacheable buffer discards the data just written, so the maintenance belongs to DMA buffers only; DMA1 and DMA2 cannot reach DTCM: no DMA buffer there; on the Cortex-M4 of a dual-core part, byte and half-word loads from FMC SDRAM can return wrong data (errata ES0445): no such buffers. Dual-core H7 ¶ The port supports the Cortex-M7 of single-core STM32H7 parts. Dual-core parts ( STM32H745xx , STM32H747xx , STM32H755xx , STM32H757xx ) are refused at configure time, and a build with CORE_CM4 stops at compile time: on the second core the EXTI pending bits are in the core-2 registers ( C2PR1 ), the port's clock and tables are per core, and the peripherals are shared between the cores.

docs.text: How the port depends on kb-core ¶ Today: a hash-locked copy of kb-core main ¶ kb-core ( kokeb-labs/kb-core ) is private and has no release tag yet, so this repository's CI cannot fetch it and cannot pin a release. Until both change, the port carries an unchanged copy of the kb-core files it builds against in third_party/kb-core (see SOUP and kb-core ): the copied commit is on kb-core's main ; tools/kb_core_snapshot.py --update refuses any other commit, and the lock records the branch and the commit; the copy is the whole cmake/ folder plus the three parts the port uses ( utils , rtos , interfaces ), their backends, the host test port and the test harness; documentation, drivers and the other parts are not copied; every configure and tools/kb_core_snapshot.py --check re-hash every file against third_party/kb-core.lock . A re-pin is one commit: --update from a kb-core checkout at the new main commit, then the full pre-flight and the firmware builds of every family. Plan: a kb-core release, fetched, never copied ¶ The copy is an interim measure. It is replaced in these steps, in order: A kb-core release tag. The port pins a tag (for example v0.3.0 once the M3 to M5 work is tagged), never a branch commit. kb-core's own MISRA and test evidence belongs to its releases, so the port's SOUP record points at that release's evidence. CI access without a copy. One of: kb-core becomes public before this port does (a public port cannot build against a private dependency anyway), or a read-only deploy key or fine-grained token for kokeb-labs/kb-core held as an organisation secret and used only by the checkout step of the shared workflows. Consumption. find_package(kb CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS interfaces rtos utils) stays the primary path (already supported by cmake/kb_port_stm32_kb_core.cmake ). The fallback becomes FetchContent_Declare(kb GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/kokeb-labs/kb-core GIT_TAG <tag commit>) with the same post-fetch git rev-parse HEAD check the HAL fetch already does ( cmake/kb_port_stm32_hal.cmake ). Records. kb-core in docs/soup.md as a pinned internal dependency with its release, and a compatibility row (port version x kb-core version) as kb-core's design foresees. A scheduled job builds the port against kb-core main to catch contract drift before a release. Removal. third_party/kb-core , third_party/kb-core.lock and tools/kb_core_snapshot.py are deleted in the same change that adds the fetch. No port code changes in any of these steps: the port uses kb-core only through its public kb/<part>/ headers.

docs.text: MISRA review of "to review" findings ¶ The MISRA scan ( ci-misra.yml ) marks a finding "to review" when its guideline's CodeQL query was found, in the tool validation of ci-tools, to report compliant code (the anomaly ids, AN-* , are in the scan's misra-findings.csv ). They do not fail the level; each needs the reviewer's check (review checklist R-FP): a real one is fixed, a false one needs no record beyond the anomaly. This page reviews the CI scan of v0.1.0-rc.1 , not the current code. No scan of the current code has been run yet; the CI MISRA job of the pull request produces it. Its "to review" list must be checked against the table below before the next release candidate: a finding whose pattern is here gets the verdict here, a new pattern is reviewed and added, and the scanned commit is written into this page. Scope ¶ Scan reviewed: the CI scan of v0.1.0-rc.1 (host and Cortex-M configurations, 25 source files each): 303 findings to review in 14 guidelines, 19 advisory violations (Rule 6.5.1 x 18, Rule 10.1.1 x 1), 10 deviated (Rule 6.7.1, DEV-001). Since that scan the port changed substantially (interrupt-driven waits, the shared state out of the boundary files, src/can_time_log.cpp split into can.cpp and time.cpp ): many of the reviewed lines no longer exist. The verdicts below are per pattern; the scan of the next release re-lists the findings, and a finding whose pattern is not in the table below is reviewed and added here before that release. Verdicts ¶ Guideline Findings Pattern found at the sites Verdict Rule 0.0.2 (invariant condition), advisory 1 Inside the expansion of __HAL_TIM_SET_AUTORELOAD (a HAL macro's constant sub-expression) False positive (anomaly): the condition belongs to the SOUP macro, not to the port Rule 0.1.1 (unnecessary write), advisory 28 The single-exit style: a local initialised to a safe default, then assigned on every branch ( uint32_t code = port_code::kOwned; if (...) { code = ...; } ) False positive (anomaly): the initial value is the defined result on the path that does not assign; kept on purpose (no uninitialised local, KB-CPP20 single exit) Rule 0.2.4 (unused limited-visibility function), advisory 9 The fdcan:: / bxcan:: helpers of the CAN boundary: one family's set is compiled per variant and reached through the family alias False positive (anomaly): each helper is called in its own family's build Rule 4.6.1 (unsequenced use and modification), required 4 ok ? Compute(..., ok) : value : the condition is sequenced before the chosen operand, so the code was well-defined False positive, fixed anyway : the three sites in adc.cpp , pwm.cpp and spi.cpp are now if statements; the CAN site is gone Rule 5.13.4 (unsigned literal suffix), required 36 Empty brace initialisers of PinId members ( PinId tx{}; ) and similar: the query reports the 0 (an octal literal of type int ) of an enumerator or default member initialiser behind them False positive (anomaly): no unsigned literal without U is written; 0 is signed Rule 6.8.4 (ref-qualified member functions), advisory 5 Accessors that return a member by const reference ( Config() , Timing() ) Reviewed, kept (advisory): the objects are non-copyable and non-movable and live for the program (drivers hold references), so a dangling reference from a temporary cannot arise in use Rule 7.0.1 (conversion from bool), required 17 A bool bound to a bool& out-parameter ( ComputeCanTiming(..., ok) ), and static_cast<void> of a bool False positive (anomaly): a reference binding and a discard are not conversions of the value Rule 7.0.2 (implicit conversion to bool), required 24 A bool& read as bool ; the HAL's FlagStatus compared with RESET False positive (anomaly): no value conversion happens Rule 7.0.5 (signedness change by promotion), required 28 Comparisons of uint8_t values with uint8_t constants ( address >= kI2cFirstAddress , config_.mode <= kMaxMode ), uint8_t shift counts ( 1U << pin.pin ), and HAL macro expansions in the boundary files False positive (anomaly): both operands are promoted alike and non-negative below 2^16, so no value or comparison result changes; the shift counts were re-checked, every one is below 32 Rule 7.0.6 (numeric assignment type mismatch), required 64 Mostly HAL constants assigned to HAL fields in the boundary and vector files ( I2C_MEMADD_SIZE_16BIT , IRQn_Type values, __HAL_RCC_* expansions); in the logic, a uint8_t member assigned a constant that fits ( mode_ = ok ? mode : 0xFFU ) and a returned kb::Status False positive (anomaly): every value fits its destination; the HAL's types are fixed by the SOUP Rule 8.2.2 (C-style casts), required 11 Brace-initialised temporaries ( uint64_t{raw} , uint32_t{1U} ) used to widen before arithmetic False positive (anomaly): list initialisation is not a functional-notation cast and cannot narrow; the port has no C-style cast ( -Wold-style-cast -Werror on every platform-free file) Rule 8.14.1 (short-circuited side effect), advisory 12 The right operand reads a register or pops a ring ( PinRead(sda) && PinRead(scl) , n < size && ring.TryPop(b) , the elapsed-time checks of the old polling loops) Real (advisory), fixed : both pins are read before the test, the ring drain and the recovery clock loop no longer short-circuit a side effect, ItmEnabled reads both registers first; the polling loops are gone Rule 8.20.1 (unsigned wrap with constant operands), advisory 56 Statistics counters ( ++stats.transfers ), the DWT elapsed-cycle difference now - last , rounding sums in 64 bits ( raw * vref + full / 2 , total + span - 1 ), and x - 1U after x >= 1 is established ( prescaler - 1U , quanta - sample ) Reviewed: counters and cycle differences wrap by design (modular arithmetic is the intent); every rounding sum and product is in 64 bits over operands below 2^32 and cannot wrap; every subtraction is guarded by its range check Rule 9.5.1 (simple legacy for ), advisory 8 Searches that stop early ( for (...; (n < max) && !ok; ++n) ) and loops over a counter with a second condition Reviewed, kept (advisory): each loop has a fixed upper bound and a counter it alone changes; the recovery loop was rewritten as a simple loop Advisory violations left ¶ Guideline Where Why it stays Rule 6.5.1 The interrupt vectors and the HAL callbacks Their names are fixed by the startup file and the HAL headers ( MISRA boundary and deviations ) Rule 10.1.1 The HAL callbacks' handle parameters The signatures are the HAL's Reviewer: the maintainer of record ( .github/CODEOWNERS ), 2026-11-14, against the CI scan of v0.1.0-rc.1 ; docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ Host tests over HAL fakes ¶ The port's logic ( src/*.cpp , one per public header) and its boundary files ( src/boundary/*.cpp , one per HAL component) are built unchanged on the host against tests/fakes/stm32 : one-line headers with the HAL's names ( stm32g4xx_hal.h , stm32f4xx_hal.h ) over one declaration file with the register blocks, handle types and macros the boundary files use, and fake_stm32_hal.cpp , which defines every HAL function they call. That is a link seam per HAL call: the tests inject any HAL_StatusTypeDef and ErrorCode into any function ( fake::Fail ), drive a small model of each peripheral (pin levels, I2C devices that ACK or NACK, the BUSY flag, SPI and UART bytes, ADC values, running timer counters, a 3-deep CAN FIFO with overrun, error counters and bus-off), stop HAL_GetTick() to prove no wait reads it, advance the DWT counter, and re-enter the port from inside a HAL call or a time read ( fake::Hook ) to prove each lock. The interrupt APIs ( *_IT ) call the port's HAL callbacks at once, as the interrupt would, and the UART model runs the port's handler while a transmit interrupt is enabled; fake::Stall holds an area's interrupts to prove every timeout and its stop-and-restore. Each variant has only the macros its family's HAL has (the F4 fake has no 7-bit UART word). The DMA boundary files ( src/boundary/dma.cpp , spi_dma.cpp , adc_stream.cpp ) are the exception: the tests link tests/dma_model/dma_model.cpp in their place, the same sdk:: calls over kb-core's host DMA-and-cache model (the files themselves are compiled over the fakes' register declarations, not linked, so the MISRA scan and clang-tidy see them) ( kb::dma::host::Machine , DmaEngine , HwRing ). kb-core's conformance suite T1 to T18 runs against the port's real classes through the adapter rigs of tests/dma_model/port_rig.hpp ; the result per case is in DMA . Test Proves kb_port_stm32_tests_g4 Every member of every type, every refusal and every HAL error path, over a G4-like device: I2C v2 (TIMINGR), FDCAN, ADC calibration; the *Ref of each contract at run time; the clock's read rule over every interleaving of its reads with the wrap interrupt ( test_clock_read.cpp ); the waits with the HAL tick stopped and with no clock at all ( test_completion.cpp ) kb_port_stm32_tests_f4 The same tests over an F4-like device: I2C v1 (ClockSpeed), bxCAN, no ADC calibration, the SR-register UART flags test_dma_conformance.cpp (in both variants) kb-core's DMA conformance suite T1 to T18 on the port, in the Maintained (AXI) and NonCacheable (D2) regions; T1, T2 and T7 also with a defect in the boundary model, which they catch test_dma.cpp , test_spi_dma.cpp , test_adc_stream.cpp The DMA layer: B31 (a flag with nothing in flight cleared, counted, no re-entry), B32 (NVIC priority read back), B33 (conversion count against the frame, one-shot fallback), the SPI order, errors, quarantine and recovery, the ADC stream's supervision, overrun, seqlock and start rules kb_port_stm32_compile_fail_* Misuse is a compile error: a *Ref of the wrong contract, a copied controller, an output pin as an input, a DTCM buffer for DMA1, a stream priority outside the implemented bits, an engine that is not DMA½, a driver frame above the staging buffers, an ADC frame that is not 16-bit samples kb_port_stm32_header_checks Each public header compiles on its own as ISO C++20 with the strict flags static_assert s in port.hpp , beside each type and in the tests Each type satisfies its concepts and converts to its *Ref ; Cycles() and CompareFor() at compile time cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DKB_PORT_STM32_BUILD_TESTS = ON && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build Local pre-flight ¶ tools/preflight.sh runs what CI runs, before a push: the kb-core copy check, clang-format 20, the tests with Clang (strict flags) and GCC at -O2, ASan and UBSan, coverage at the high level's limits (lines 85 %, branches 75 %), lizard (CCN 15, 60 lines, 6 parameters), clang-tidy 20, misra_lint --strict , the handbook check, the layering check and the platform-free build. clang-tidy's configuration is checked with --verify-config , and a clang-tidy that reports a configuration error fails the step (the host job's clang-tidy 18 once rejected a key and reported nothing). docs.text: Thread safety ¶ The port follows kb-core's thread models (kb-core docs/design/handlers.md ): a bus is either owned by one task (model O) or shared through a guarded facade (model G). The port is safe under both, because every shared resource has its own bounded lock, a kb::rtos::Mutex taken with TryLockFor(timeout) . Object Lock Held for When not had in time I2cController One per controller One transfer (plus a probe with nack_probe , and a restore or recovery after a failure) Busy , nothing sent SpiBus One per instance, shared by its devices One frame (all its chunks) or one device change Busy , nothing clocked Uart One for the reader, one for the writer One Read , one Write ; SetBaud takes both Busy AdcChannel One per ADC instance, shared by its channels One conversion Busy CanController One for sending, one for receiving One Send or one Receive with its wait; Recover takes the send lock Busy OutputPin , InputPin None One register access (BSRR, IDR); Toggle masks interrupts for its read-modify-write PwmChannel None Register writes; one object per channel, used from one context; timer ownership changes with interrupts masked Clock , BusyWait , log sinks None Clock::Now is lock-free and interrupt-safe; UartLogSink uses the Uart 's writer lock Rules: Create, then share. EnsureReady() creates the object's lock; call it once from one context before the object is used by others. Later calls are idempotent and cheap. No lock across calls. A lock is never held when a call returns, so no caller can block another longer than one transfer plus its timeout. Interrupts never take a lock. Shared tables change with interrupts masked. Pin claims, the EXTI line table (callback and context are atomic, written with interrupts masked, so a handler always sees a callback with its own context), timer ownership and the ADC instances' channel counts are changed only inside a few-instruction section with interrupts masked (PRIMASK saved and restored), never a kb::rtos critical section (which, before the scheduler, could leave BASEPRI raised). LastError(), LastFailure() and Stats() ¶ LastError() is the status and vendor code of the most recent call on the object by any task ; LastFailure() (I2C) is the failure kind of the most recent transfer; Stats() are the object's counters. They are not per task. Under the owner-task model (one task per bus, kb-core's default for real-time buses) the owner reads its own call's detail. Under a shared model, another task's call may have replaced the record between a call and the read of its detail: rely on the returned kb::Status there, and read LastError() only for diagnostics. - Under a model G facade the handler's lock is taken first, then the port's lock (kb-core's fixed order); the port's lock is the inner one and never waits for a handler. With KB_RTOS=NONE (bare metal, and the host tests) the locks still exist: a call made while the lock is held (from an interrupt, or nested) is refused with Busy after its timeout instead of corrupting the transfer, which the host tests use to prove every lock path. docs.text: How the port waits ¶ Every call that waits for hardware is bounded, measured on the port's own clock, and asleep under an RTOS. No wait of the port reads HAL_GetTick() , and none spins the CPU at the caller's priority. The rule ¶ Wait Started by Ended by Bounded by I2C transfer HAL_I2C_Master_Seq_Transmit_IT / _Seq_Receive_IT / _Master_Transmit_IT (probe) The HAL's completion or error callback I2cConfig::timeout SPI chunk HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT / HAL_SPI_Transmit_IT The HAL's completion or error callback SpiDeviceConfig::timeout per chunk UART write The transmit-empty interrupt (the port's own handler) The last byte handed over, or transmit-complete with RS-485 UartConfig::write_timeout UART read — The receive interrupt (a byte or an error) The Read() timeout WaitTxDone() The transmit-complete interrupt Transmit-complete Its timeout ADC conversion HAL_ADC_Start_IT HAL_ADC_ConvCpltCallback or HAL_ADC_ErrorCallback AdcConfig::conversion_timeout CAN receive — The RX FIFO 0 interrupt (into the port's ring) The Receive() timeout CAN send (no free slot) — The transmit-complete interrupt The Send() timeout CAN bus-off recovery Recover() The controller back on the bus (checked after each pause) The Recover() timeout Locks — kb::rtos::Mutex The object's lock timeout Every timeout, configured or per call, is at most kMaxTimeout (2 s); a longer one, and HAL_MAX_DELAY , is refused with InvalidArgument . 2 s leaves room for a secure element that stretches SCL for several hundred milliseconds, and is short enough that a failing bus cannot hold callers for long. A caller that must wait longer loops. Deadline and Completion ¶ Deadline ( completion.hpp ) measures a budget on the port's Clock (TIM2 or TIM5) once one has been started, and on the DWT cycle counter (extended to 64 bits before any division, never written) before that. A second, independent bound ends a wait even if that time source stops (an application that re-initialises or gates the clock's timer, for example): under FreeRTOS ( KB_RTOS=FREERTOS , CMake defines KB_PORT_STM32_RTOS_BLOCKS ), the time slept on the RTOS tick: each slice that ended by its timeout lasted at least the slice, so the deadline expires after budget + kWaitSliceMs of slept slices (a 50 ms wait at most 60 ms of RTOS time); under kb-core's none backend, where a take cannot sleep, the poll count: (budget in ms + 1) x kDeadlinePollsPerMs polls. Completion is armed by the task, completed from the interrupt (or the HAL callback) with the vendor code, and waited for in slices of at most kWaitSliceMs (10 ms) on a kb::rtos::Semaphore : FreeRTOS ( KB_RTOS=FREERTOS ): the task blocks in the semaphore take until the interrupt gives it or the slice ends. It uses no CPU while it waits, and lower-priority tasks run. none backend ( KB_RTOS=NONE , bare metal): kb-core's none backend has no scheduler; its take cannot block and returns at once (its SleepFor does not sleep on silicon either: its tick is a fake counter). The wait becomes a poll of the completion flag, bounded by the Deadline on the port clock or the DWT and by the poll cap. That is the documented fallback: correct and bounded, but it occupies the CPU for the wait, as any bare-metal wait does. On a timeout the operation is stopped before the call returns: an I2C transfer has its handle restored (and the peripheral reset if BUSY stays set), an SPI transfer is aborted ( HAL_SPI_Abort , a counted wait in the HAL) and the peripheral initialised again before the next frame, an ADC conversion is stopped ( HAL_ADC_Stop_IT ), a UART write has its transmit interrupts disabled. What still depends on the HAL tick ¶ The HAL's own initialisation and stop paths wait on HAL_GetTick() for single hardware acknowledgements that take microseconds on healthy silicon: HAL_UART_Init (TEACK/REACK), HAL_ADC_Start_IT 's first enable (ADRDY) and HAL_ADC_Stop_IT , HAL_FDCAN_Init / HAL_CAN_Init and their start and stop (INIT acknowledge). The port does not replace the HAL there; instead: Uart , CanController and AdcChannel refuse EnsureReady() with NotReady (port code kHalTickStopped ) when the HAL time base does not advance within two HAL tick periods ( HAL_GetTickFreq() ) and at least 25 ms, measured on the DWT, so a HAL tick advanced at 100 Hz (from an RTOS tick hook) is accepted; Uart::SetBaud() and the FDCAN restart in CanController::Recover() check it again before their HAL calls; call EnsureReady() , Release() and SetBaud() from task context, never with interrupts masked, never inside a critical section, and never from an interrupt; under an RTOS, give the HAL its time base from a source that runs whenever tasks run (see Getting started ). The I2C and SPI initialisations and every transfer do not use the HAL tick. Two waits spin the CPU at the caller's priority by design, both bounded and outside the transfers: the HAL's I2C v1 (F4) busy-flag wait at the start of a transfer (a counted loop, about 25 ms of iterations, only when BUSY is set), and the HAL time-base check of EnsureReady() (ends at the first tick, at most 25 ms or two tick periods). Later: kb-core's asynchronous Start/Poll contract ¶ kb-core is adding an asynchronous Start/Poll contract for hot paths (its design, section 16: "a non-blocking form" for bus calls). The port is built so that it maps onto it without a new HAL path: every interface call is already split into a start ( sdk::I2cStartTransmit , sdk::SpiStart , sdk::AdcStart , the transmit-interrupt enable) and an end signalled by an interrupt into a Completion ; Start() would arm the Completion and call the same start; Poll() would return Done() and, when done, the result from Code() (and Value() for the ADC), without waiting; a timeout would be the caller's deadline on the same port clock, and the same stop-and-restore runs when the caller gives up; the blocking calls stay, written as Start() followed by Completion::Wait() . The change is then local to the platform-free files ( i2c.cpp , spi.cpp , adc.cpp , pwm.cpp , uart.cpp , can.cpp ); the boundary files and the HAL callbacks stay as they are.
